candidate.answerReason: Writing \(t=k+2\ge3\), the exponent of \(2\) is \(t\) for \(t<6\), is \(6\) for \(t>6\), and is \(7\) for \(t=6\). Thus the maximum is \(7\), attained at \(k=4\).

methods.label: Factor until the remaining factor is odd
methods.explanation:
The digit positions give
\[
I_k=10^{k+2}+64.
\]
Put \(t=k+2\), so \(t\) is an integer at least \(3\). Since \(10^t=2^t5^t\) and \(64=2^6\), compare \(t\) with \(6\). Once a power of \(2\) has been factored out and the remaining factor is odd, its exponent is exactly \(N(k)\).

If \(3\le t<6\), then
\[
I_k=2^t\left(5^t+2^{6-t}\right).
\]
The factor in parentheses is odd plus even, hence odd. Thus \(N(k)=t\le5\).

If \(t>6\), then
\[
I_k=2^6\left(2^{t-6}5^t+1\right).
\]
The factor in parentheses is even plus one, hence odd. Thus \(N(k)=6\).

The remaining case is \(t=6\). Here
\[
I_k=2^6(5^6+1)
=2^6(15626)
=2^7(7813).
\]
Since \(7813\) is odd, \(N(k)=7\).

These cases cover every allowed \(k\). The maximum is therefore \(\boxed{7}\), attained when \(k=t-2=4\), choice B.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is determining and maximizing the exponent of a prime in an integer. Parity certifies that no further factors of two remain, while powers of products rewrite the decimal power. The three cases prove an upper bound for all inputs and exhibit an input attaining it.
